split_question: Should EU students pay the same university fees as UK students, if that helps keep the wider trade deal with the EU?
angles: say yes to home fees and pay for the gap from public money
say no to home fees and keep the rest of the deal
trade it: home fees only for a fair share back, such as UK students' places or costs in the EU
facts_for_writers: Before Brexit EU students paid the same fees as home students, now up to £9,790 a year; since January 2020 they have paid international fees of up to £38,000 a year (s4).
EU officials want students from the 27 member states to pay UK home rates and have said the rest of the deal depends on it; the UK disputes that link (s4).
The joint statement commits both sides to work towards a tuition-fee agreement that would cover all students from the other side, to conclude within six months of the summit (s4).
The Russell Group warns that any cut would put pressure on UK student places and take money out of higher education; the NUS welcomes lower fees (s4).
The government says the whole package could add up to 0.5% to UK GDP by 2040, about £17 billion a year (s1).
